function: Near-field XL-MIMO channel estimation: a learned denoiser refines the least-squares estimate of the channel matrix obtained from pilots (pp. 4, 6).
system: mmWave 60 GHz uplink XL-MIMO, near-field spherical waves, ULAs with Nr=256 receive and Nt=8 transmit antennas, DFT pilot beams; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: MsSAN: three-layer encoder-decoder transformer with low-complexity spatial attention, supervised offline training with MSE loss and SGD, input is the LS estimate (pp. 6-7, 10).
data_channel: Own dataset: extended Saleh-Valenzuela near-field model, 2x10^4 samples, 4:1 split (p. 10, Table I); QuaDRiGa BERLIN_UMi_NLOS dataset, 28 GHz, 128x16 antennas (p. 12, Table IV).
test_conditions: Train: r in [3, dR] m, L~Poisson(6), SNR -10 to 10 dB, 4:1 split (p. 10). Test: held-out set; r 5-200 m beyond dR, and QuaDRiGa data (p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, LMMSE, OMP with polar codebook; learned: CNN, LISTA, classical transformer (TF); ablation: single-scale SAN (p. 10).
metrics: NMSE (main) and spectral efficiency with MRT downlink; CRLB as bound (pp. 10-11).
complexity: Order O(3^2*B*Nr*Nt*C + B*Nr*Nt*C^2), linear in array size, versus TF O(B*Nr^2*Nt^2*C) and LMMSE O(Nr^3*Nt^3) (p. 10, Table III p. 11); no runtime.
openness: none: no code or data link or release statement; datasets are generated with the extended Saleh-Valenzuela model and QuaDRiGa (pp. 10, 12).
q1_support: p. 12: "we apply QuaDRiGa platform to generate the cluster channel dataset based on the realistic measurement scenario" BERLIN_UMi_NLOS (Table IV), and MsSAN is evaluated on it in Fig. 12; the main data are a custom extended Saleh-Valenzuela model (p. 10). Training on the QuaDRiGa data is implied, not stated.
q2_support: p. 12: "the evaluated neural networks are trained only on data within the near-field region during offline training phase"; training uses r in [3, dR] (p. 10) while the tested distances reach 200 m beyond dR = 174.25 m (Fig. 11), i.e. the far field.
q3_support: p. 10: "Deep CNN-based channel estimation [33], [34], [37], termed as CNN", with LISTA [36] and TF [40], [41] as learned baselines and "LS and LMMSE" and OMP as non-learned; NMSE comparison in Fig. 9 (p. 11).
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall complexity of the proposed MsSAN for XL-MIMO channel estimation is the order of" O(3^2 B Nr Nt C) + O(B Nr Nt C^2); Table III (p. 11) lists the online complexity of all schemes.
q5_support: p. 10: "the channel dataset is generated by employing extended Saleh-Valenzuela model"; the QuaDRiGa data are also generated by the authors (p. 12). Missing: no code or data link, no release statement, no public or measured dataset.
notes: Area 2: channel estimation in XL-MIMO. A RIS appears only in the related work (p. 2) and not in the system, so ris is 0. q1: the main experiments use a custom extended Saleh-Valenzuela simulator, which alone would not count; q1 is 1 only because of the QuaDRiGa BERLIN_UMi_NLOS experiment (Fig. 12, Table IV), and the paper does not say in words that the networks are trained on it, so the reviewer should confirm. q2: Fig. 11 relies on the statement that training used only near-field data while test distances extend to 200 m beyond dR; Fig. 12 and Fig. 13 (paths 2-10) are not used because their training conditions are not stated. q5: QuaDRiGa is a public simulator, but the paper releases no dataset or code.
